units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
He nods affably to Malone and goes out through the little gate in the paling.
very civilly.
I am so sorry, Mr Malone, if that man has been rude to you. But what can we do? He is our chauffeur.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Your what?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: The driver of our automobile. He can drive a motor car at seventy miles an hour, and mend it when it breaks down. We are dependent on our motor cars; and our motor cars are dependent on him; so of course we are dependent on him.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I've noticed, madam, that every thousand dollars an Englishman gets seems to add one to the number of people he's dependent on. However, you needn't apologize for your man: I made him talk on purpose. By doing so I learnt that you're staying here in Grannida with a party of English, including my son Hector.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: conversationally.
Yes. We intended to go to Nice; but we had to follow a rather eccentric member of our party who started first and came here. Won't you sit down?
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: She clears the nearest chair of the two books on it.
impressed by this attention.
Thank you.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: He sits down, examining her curiously as she goes to the iron table to put down the books.
When she turns to him again, he says.
Miss Robinson, I believe?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: sitting down.
Yes.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Taking a letter from his pocket.
Your note to Hector runs as follows
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Violet is unable to repress a start.
He pauses quietly to take out and put on his spectacles, which have gold rims.

: "Dearest: they have all gone to the Alhambra for the afternoon. I have shammed headache and have the garden all to myself. Jump into Jack's motor: Straker will rattle you here in a jiffy. Quick, quick, quick. Your loving Violet."
units.name: MALONE

units.text: He looks at her; but by this time she has recovered herself, and meets his spectacles with perfect composure.
He continues slowly.

Now I don't know on what terms young people associate in English society; but in America that note would be considered to imply a very considerable degree of affectionate intimacy between the parties.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Yes: I know your son very well, Mr Malone. Have you any objection?
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: somewhat taken aback.
No, no objection exactly. Provided it is understood that my son is altogether dependent on me, and that I have to be consulted in any important step he may propose to take.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: I am sure you would not be unreasonable with him, Mr Malone.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I hope not, Miss Robinson; but at your age you might think many things unreasonable that don't seem so to me.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: with a little shrug.
Oh well, I suppose there's no use our playing at cross purposes, Mr Malone. Hector wants to marry me.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I inferred from your note that he might. Well, Miss Robinson, he is his own master; but if he marries you he shall not have a rap from me.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: He takes off his spectacles and pockets them with the note.
with some severity.
That is not very complimentary to me, Mr Malone.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I say nothing against you, Miss Robinson: I daresay you are an amiable and excellent young lady. But I have other views for Hector.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Hector may not have other views for himself, Mr Malone.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Possibly not. Then he does without me: that's all. I daresay you are prepared for that. When a young lady writes to a young man to come to her quick, quick, quick, money seems nothing and love seems everything.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: sharply.
I beg your pardon, Mr Malone: I do not think anything so foolish. Hector must have money.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: staggered.
Oh, very well, very well. No doubt he can work for it.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: What is the use of having money if you have to work for it?
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: She rises impatiently.
It's all nonsense, Mr Malone: you must enable your son to keep up his position. It is his right.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: grimly.
I should not advise you to marry him on the strength of that right, Miss Robinson.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Violet, who has almost lost her temper, controls herself with an effort; unclenches her fingers; and resumes her seat with studied tranquillity and reasonableness.
